### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `62e407f7ee9b3c8a7257a8824837e1b5099e53c1` — the merge of head `99213d3feb5592466b82b2ad05d5aede994db3c6` into base `895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 62e407f7ee9b3c8a7257a8824837e1b5099e53c1 && git checkout 62e407f7ee9b3c8a7257a8824837e1b5099e53c1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 99213d3feb5592466b82b2ad05d5aede994db3c6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87 && git merge --no-ff 99213d3feb5592466b82b2ad05d5aede994db3c6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 895783a1e864e0fe629c56b3c6315771ca87bf87
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2414ce53fb908b044eca6ba722b2637902da758c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/io-node-config.zod.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/http-nodes.ts + packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-connector.ts

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: unchanged, right. `HttpConfigSchema.method` is still `z.string().optional()` with the same `.describe()`; the hunk is TSDoc only. No `json-schema`, `authorable-surface` or `api-surface` path is in the diff. `Spec property liveness`, `Type Check · consumer gates` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are `success` on this head.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. Nothing an author can write moves.
- Public surface: one change, and the PR names it wrong. `@objectstack/spec` ships `src/**/*.zod.ts` (`files[]`), so the edited TSDoc is shipped bytes of the next spec tarball. See ②.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no. The `skip-changeset` label is wrong on this head; a `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/spec` is owed.

- `packages/spec/package.json`: not `private`, `files` lists `src/**/*.zod.ts`. The diff rewrites five TSDoc lines in `io-node-config.zod.ts`. The released 18.5.0 text quotes code that no longer exists, which the review checklist calls a published defect ("spec 发运 `src/**/*.zod.ts`,假 TSDoc 即缺陷"). Correcting it is a fix in a released package: AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 gives it `patch`, "never none, and never `skip-changeset`: that label is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package". The checklist adds that size is not the criterion and that a missing changeset does not queue.
- `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/connector-openapi`: not `private`, but `files` is `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. Both edits are line comments inside function bodies. They reach no `.js` and no `.d.ts`, and the shared tsup config drops `sourcesContent`. Nothing is owed for these two.
- The PR body's reason ("nothing this PR changes publishes behaviour") tests behaviour; the rule tests shipped bytes. The changeset corrections moved to #33896 are a different matter (two released CHANGELOG entries) and do not cover this TSDoc.
- Gate verdict: `Check Changeset` is `failure` on the run that judged the diff (13:20Z); the later `skipped` run is the label's exemption, not a pass.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation "stale PR body": answered. The body on this head reads `Fixes #33663`, `Fixes #33655`; `PR-body guards` is `success`.
- Deviation "no changeset, area applies `skip-changeset`": answered wrongly. See M1.
- Deviation "repo-wide lint and spec dependents not run locally": answered by `Lint · ESLint`, `Test Core` (8 of 8) and `TypeScript Type Check`, all `success`.
- Deviation "type-check-debt not measured locally": answered by `Type Check · debt ledger`, `success`.
- `open_questions[0]` (connector pull door): answered. The area ruled option C; #33894 is open and carries it.
- Out-of-scope findings: #33895 (durable GET through the outbox) and #33896 (released CHANGELOG amendment) are both open.

### ④ Design judgment

`io-node-config.zod.ts`, `method` TSDoc, read against `http-nodes.ts` at this head. Every sentence holds.
- "run with `{ url, durable: true }` it sends `POST`, enqueued on a ready outbox or sent on the no-outbox fallback alike": true. One `method` value feeds `enqueueHttp`, the awaited `sendInline` and the background `sendInline` on the save path.
- "`http-nodes.ts` resolves the verb once, from the authored `method` and `durable`": true (`cfg.method ?? (durable ? 'POST' : 'GET')`).
- "a static `.default('GET')` ... the durable `POST` would never apply again": true. The executor reads the parsed config, so the `??` could not fire.

`http-nodes.ts`, fallback comment, read against `sendInline`, `deliveryBody`, `sendOnce` and both outbox signers.
- Same verb: true. No body: inline sends none and signs `''`; the outbox gets `body ?? {}` and sends and signs `'{}'`: true. String body: inline `JSON.stringify`, outbox verbatim: true. `Content-Type: application/json`: only `sendOnce` sets it: true.
- N1 (nit) — "the outbox's bytes for an object body only" is too narrow. An array, number or boolean literal also serialises to the same bytes on both arms. "For a non-string body" is the exact wording.
- N2 (nit) — the same file's header still says "the durable outbox enqueues exactly the request the inline call would send" (about line 64). That is the over-claim card #33655 N2 asked to correct "where it is restated", and it now contradicts the new comment. Not shipped (`dist` only). It can ride the fix round for M1.

`openapi-connector.ts`, comment above the `required.push`, read against `buildInputSchema`. All three clauses hold: `path` is pushed when it declares a property; any section is pushed when `sec.required` is non-empty; a section emitted only for an unresolved `$ref` has no properties, hence no `required` entries, and is not pushed.

M1 (must-fix) — `skip-changeset` is a false declaration on this head. Remove the label and add a `patch` changeset naming `@objectstack/spec`, whose body carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` and states the corrected `HttpConfigSchema.method` TSDoc.
